tACK 9b78edce891f717c562c8c62d082c3a3facb43fa

On your `fallback_locktime` question: which value is kept does not change the transaction. `GetUniqueID()` hashes nLockTime, so where both fallbacks set it and differ, `Merge` returns false. Different fallbacks get through only when a required lock time on an input sets the merged nLockTime, and then the fallback is not used.

I combined 5000 random PSBTv2 pairs in both orders with `combinepsbt` and with btclib-wallet. Both refused all 155 pairs with different fallbacks and no required lock time. In the 1342 accepted pairs with different fallbacks, the order changed the kept fallback but never nLockTime ([script and output](https://gist.github.com/fametrano/ceb061d73c60dd5d3c7370fbb1341c8d/6235cac8f1a2a0715d85843797afbe9087530143)).
@nebula-21 do you want to take @polespinasa's suggestion?

yup took the suggestion to improve readability :)

reACK 7b124184394e016d6e3c119c50ff08d1512dfab9

The only change since 9b78edce is polespinasa's suggested diff, applied as posted: the bit indices of `m_tx_modifiable` become named constants. Their values match BIP370 (bit 0 inputs modifiable, bit 1 outputs modifiable, bit 2 has SIGHASH_SINGLE) and the bits `psbt.cpp` and `decodepsbt` read. `psbt_tests` pass on this head, and no non-test code changed, so the earlier `combinepsbt` comparison still holds.
